name: insolvia-workspace
//: Root of the Insolvia npm workspace. NOT a shippable package — it declares
the members and pins the shared toolchain.
The member list is EXPLICIT and must stay that way — never `packages/*`.
apps/insolvia_marketing is deliberately NOT a member: globbing (or adding
it) would put it on this root's lockfile, and its own lockfile is what
proves a clean registry install works.
THE DESIGN SYSTEM IS NOT HERE. @insolvia-ai/design-system and
@insolvia-ai/tokens live in github.com/insolvia-ai/design-system and are
consumed BY PUBLISHED VERSION, like any third-party dependency. They were
workspace members until the extraction, and the app read the design
system's SOURCE through the resulting symlink — so a change was live for
the app and invisible to marketing at the same time. Do not add them back
as members, and do not add a `file:`/`link:` path to a local checkout:
that recreates exactly the split channel the extraction removed. To try an
unpublished change, publish a prerelease from that repo.
CAUTION — Node resolution walks UP the tree. A missing dependency in
apps/insolvia_marketing can resolve from this root's node_modules and pass
CI, then fail in a clean install. It keeps its own package-lock.json and
its own CI job installs from it, which is what catches this — do not
consolidate it here.

//tokens: The token SOURCE is no longer here — tokens.json and its generator left
with the design system. What remains is the one output that was always
this repo's own: Cognito's managed-login branding under infra/, which is
reconciled against the installed @insolvia-ai/tokens rather than
rendered from a tokens.json we no longer have.
So `tokens:check` still answers a real question — 'do the sign-in page's
colours match the tokens version this repo has installed?' — and now
also fails when a tokens bump lands without the branding being
regenerated. To change a colour: change it in the design-system repo,
publish, bump @insolvia-ai/tokens here, then `npm run tokens`.
Run with plain `node`, no loader and no build step: Node >=24 strips
TypeScript types natively, so the tool stays dependency-free.
//lint: Fans out per member rather than running ESLint once from the root, and
there is deliberately NO `eslint.config.js` at the repo root — the rules
live in `eslint.base.js`, which each member re-exports. ESLint discovers
a flat config by walking UP from its cwd, so a root one is also found by
any subdirectory with its own ESLint setup, once breaking a version-gated
package's own ESLint 8 gate. Read eslint.base.js before changing this.
scripts.lint: npm run lint --workspaces --if-present && npm run lint:tool
//tool: `tool/` is not a workspace member — it is one script this repo runs
against its own infra, with no package boundary to justify. It still
gets linted and typechecked like everything else, which is what these
two entries buy; without them the fan-out above would skip it silently.
`lint:tool` cd's first, and must keep doing so. ESLint resolves its flat
config from its CWD, not from the paths it is given, so `eslint tool`
from the root finds no config at all and dies — there is deliberately
none at the repo root (see eslint.base.js). Running from inside tool/ is
the same shape as every workspace member's own `eslint .`.
//app: The app's own scripts (`build`, `web`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`) live in
apps/insolvia_app/package.json and are a contract with app-*.yml. These two
are conveniences for a developer at the repo root: `app` starts the dev
server on port 3000 (the exact-match Cognito origin), `app:build` produces
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present && npm run typecheck:tool
//ci: The whole local gate: token drift, format, lint, typecheck, test. Mirrors
what the CI workflows run per area, so `npm run ci` green locally is a
fair predictor of a green PR.
scripts.ci: npm run tokens:check && npm run format && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test

//devDependencies: ESLint/Prettier versions match apps/insolvia_marketing deliberately — a
second ESLint major in the repo would be a trap, not a choice.
TypeScript is 5.9 rather than the 7.x line: `erasableSyntaxOnly` (5.8+) is
the feature this workspace depends on, and adopting the rewritten 7.x
compiler would be a deliberate upgrade of its own, not a default.
